latest_release.body:
# TorchTitan 0.4.0

TorchTitan 0.4.0 aligns with PyTorch 2.15, expands model coverage, improves large-scale MoE training, and unifies core training and TitanRL on a shared engine.

These highlights cover changes since 0.3.0. For broader updates and benchmarks, see [TorchTitan Update: New SOTA Models, Performance at Scale, TitanRL](https://pytorch.org/blog/torchtitan-update-new-sota-models-performance-at-scale-titanrl/).

## New model implementations

- **Muse Spark Open:** Adds the 816B-A42B model, including text and vision/audio configurations. Multimodal CUDA graphs remain unsupported. ([#5420](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5420))
- **Kimi K3:** Hybrid KDA/MLA attention, LatentMoE, and vision support, with tensor/sequence and expert parallelism plus a dedicated pipeline implementation for attention residuals. ([#4025](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/4025), [#4312](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/4312))
- **DeepSeek V4:** Initial Flash/Pro support with sparse attention, indexer loss, optional multi-token prediction, and debug recipes. Full-scale checkpoint and convergence validation remain outstanding. ([#3634](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/3634), [#4835](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/4835))

## Training performance and memory

- **Dist-MoE integration:** Fuses expert dispatch, computation, and combine. DeepSeek V3 BF16/MXFP8 recipes for NVIDIA SM100+ GPUs include fused MLA and SwiGLU. ([#4541](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/4541), [#4542](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/4542))
- **Low-precision training:** MXFP8 gains FSDP-managed prepared weights and fused weight-gradient accumulation across microbatches. Experimental NVFP4 support extends to grouped MoE linear layers. Both paths require supported Blackwell hardware and their respective optional dependencies. ([#4203](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/4203), [#4911](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/4911), [#4821](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/4821))
- **Local compilation:** `model.local_compile_regions` selects functions such as SwiGLU, RoPE, and gated RMSNorm for independent compilation and kernel fusion with `torch.compile`. ([#4894](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/4894), [#4931](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/4931), [#4985](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/4985), [#5026](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5026))
- **Faster router and LM-head layers:** `HiMidLoLinear` uses BF16 matrix multiplications with FP32 outputs. Its backward pass combines two or three BF16 parts of each FP32 output gradient, improving accuracy over a single BF16 cast. ([#4923](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/4923))
- **CUDA graphs and pipeline memory:** Adds pipeline forward/backward capture, shared training/validation graph memory, and per-microbatch-group replay, plus controls for FSDP parameter residency and unshard lookahead. ([#4493](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/4493), [#5241](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5241), [#4592](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/4592))
- **Context parallelism:** Adds Ulysses support for standard and variable-length attention, improves MLA communication, and adds native context-parallel paths for Qwen3.5 Gated DeltaNet and Kimi K3 KDA. ([#4450](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/4450), [#4760](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/4760), [#5184](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5184))
- **Activation rematerialization:** `torch_remat` controls activation saving and recomputation by region. DeepEP dispatch preserves token order during recomputation, preventing incorrect MoE gradients. ([#4497](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/4497), [#5115](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5115))
- **FlexShard / DistMuon:** Extends optimizer-compute layouts with variable-sized `BlockShard` partitions and BF16 redistribution

**A PyTorch-native platform for pretraining and post-training generative AI models at scale** [![arXiv](https://img.shields.io/badge/arXiv-2410.06511-b31b1b.svg)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.06511) [![ICLR](https://img.shields.io/badge/ICLR-2025-violet.svg)](https://iclr.cc/virtual/2025/poster/29620) [![devlogs](https://img.shields.io/badge/PyTorch-DevLog-DE3412.svg)](https://docs.pytorch.org/devlogs/) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-BSD_3--Clause-lightgrey.svg)](./LICENSE) [![pip](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/torchtitan?color=blue)](https://pypi.org/project/torchtitan/) [![conda](https://img.shields.io/conda/vn/conda-forge/torchtitan?color=green)](https://anaconda.org/conda-forge/torchtitan) [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Models](#supported-models) · [Features](#features) · [RL](torchtitan/rl/README.md) · [Docs](#documentation) · [Contributing](#contributing)
`torchtitan` is a clean-room, PyTorch-native implementation of large-scale training. One readable codebase takes a model from pretraining through supervised fine-tuning to reinforcement learning, composing FSDP, tensor, pipeline, context, and expert parallelism without rewriting the model. - **Composable parallelism.** Models declare how they shard; FSDP2, TP, PP, CP, and EP stack into N-D layouts through `DeviceMesh` and DTensor. - **Built for research.** Minimal, hackable code; every run is a Python [recipe](torchtitan/config/README.md) you can read, copy, and modify. - **Pretraining to RL in one stack.** [TitanRL](torchtitan/rl/README.md) runs the same model definitions and kernels in the trainer and in vLLM generation, with a bitwise-reproducible batch-invariant mode. - **Frontier models and techniques.** DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, gpt-oss, Llama, and FLUX, with MXFP8/NVFP4 low precision, Dist-MoE, CUDA graphs, and more. > [!NOTE] > `torchtitan` is under active development. To use the latest features, use a > recent PyTorch nightly. ## Latest news - **[2026/08]** [TitanRL](torchtitan/rl) is a hackable RL stack for scaling and debugging. It reuses TorchTitan model definitions and kernels across training and vLLM generation and supports batch-invariant mode. - **[2025/11]** AMD released an [optimized fork](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/torchtitan-amd/tree/main) of `torchtitan` for AMD GPUs. - **[2025/10]** We released `torchtitan` [v0.2.0](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/releases). - **[2025/10]** SkyPilot now supports `torchtitan`! See the [tutorial](https://docs.skypilot.co/en/latest/examples/training/torchtitan.html).
Older news - **[2025/07]** We published [instructions](torchtitan/models/README.md) on how to add a model to `torchtitan`. - **[2025/04]** Our paper was accepted by [ICLR 2025](https://iclr.cc/virtual/2025/poster/29620). - **[2024/12]** GPU MODE [lecture](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VYWRjcUqW6w) on torchtitan. - **[2024/07]** [Presentation](https://pytorch2024.sched.com/event/1fHn3) at PyTorch Conference 2024.
## Quick start **1. Install** with a PyTorch nightly (Python 3.11+). Replace `cu132` with your CUDA or ROCm build. ```bash git clone https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan && cd torchtitan pip install --pre torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/nightly/cu132 pip install -r requirements.txt ``` **2. Train a debug model.** It uses the tokenizer bundled with the tests, so no download is needed. ```bash NGPU=1 ./run_train.sh # Llama 3 debug model, 10 steps ``` **3. Train a real model.** Download the tokenizer (Llama weights require [access on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B)), then select a recipe by module and function name: ```bash python scripts/download_hf_assets.py --repo_id meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B --assets tokenizer --hf_token=... MODULE=torchtitan_recipes.models.llama3 CONFIG=llama3_8b ./run_train.sh # 8 GPUs ``` **4. Make it yours.** A recipe is a Python function returning a complete config, so changing a run means writing a function, not passing flags: ```python # my_recipes.py from torchtitan_recipes.models.llama3 import llama3_8b def llama3_8b_tp2(): config = llama3_8b() config.parallelism.tensor_parallel_degree = 2 return config ``` ```bash MODULE=my_recipes CONFIG=llama3_8b_tp2 ./run_train.sh ``` See the [configuration guide](torchtitan/config/README.md) for the full model, and [`torchtitan_recipes`](torchtitan_recipes/README.md) for the verified recipes. ## Supported models | Model | Sizes | Modality | Verified recipes | RL | | --- | --- | --- | --- | :---: | | [Llama 3](torchtitan/models/llama3) | 1B – 405B | Text | `llama3_8b`, `llama3_70b` | ✅ | | [Qwen3](torchtitan/models/qwen3) | 0.6B – 32B dense; 30B-A3B, 235B-A22B MoE | Text | `qwen3_14b` | ✅ | | [Qwen3.5](torchtitan/models/qwen3_5) / [3.6](torchtitan/models/qwen3_6) / [3.8](torchtitan/models/qwen3_8) | 0.8B – 397B-A17B; 2.4T-A95B (3.8) | Text, vision | | ✅ text | | [DeepSeek V3](torchtitan/models/deepseek_v3) | 16B, 236B, 671B | Text | `deepseek_v3_671b` (+ Dist-MoE, NVFP4) | | | [DeepSeek V4](torchtitan/models/deepseek_v4) | Flash, Pro | Text | | Soon | | [gpt-oss](torchtitan/models/gpt_oss) | 20B, 120B | Text | | ✅ | | [Kimi K2.7](torchtitan/models/kimi_k2_7) | Moonlight-16B-A3B, Kimi-VL-A3B, K2.5 | Text, vision | | | | [Kimi K3](torchtitan/models/kimi_k3) | K3 | Text, vision | | Soon | | [Muse Glimmer](torchtitan/models/muse_glimmer) | 30B | Text, vision | `muse_glimmer_30b` | ✅ | | [Muse-Spark-Open](torchtitan/models/muse_spark) | 816B-A42B | Text, vision, audio | `muse_spark_816b_a42b_dist_moe_bf16_spmd_256` | ✅ text | | [FLUX](torchtitan/models/flux) | dev, schnell | Text-to-image | `flux_dev`, `flux_schnell` | | Every model has debug configurations exercised in CI. Verified recipes have been run in training, convergence, or performance workflows. To add a model, see the [model guide](torchtitan/models/README.md). ## Features
**Parallelism** - [FSDP2](torchtitan/distributed/FSDP.md), HSDP, and DDP - Tensor parallel, including async TP - [Pipeline parallel](torchtitan/distributed/PIPELINE_PARALLEL.md): 1F1B, Interleaved 1F1B, GPipe, and other `torch.distributed.pipelining` schedules - Context parallel: all-gather KV and Ulysses - Expert parallel with DeepEP / HybridEP dispatch - [Dist-MoE](torchtitan/models/common/dist_moe/README.md): fused dispatch, expert compute, and combine on Blackwell **Memory and performance** - [Activation checkpointing](torchtitan/distributed/REMAT.md): full, selective, and regional - Regional `torch.compile` and CUDA graphs - [MXFP8](torchtitan/quantization/mxfp8/README.md) and [NVFP4](torchtitan/quantization/nvfp4/README.md) training - FlashAttention 3/4, FlexAttention, and varlen attention - [BF16 optimizer states](torchtitan/components/optim/BF16_OPTIMIZER_STATES.md) and FSDP CPU offload **Training** - [Grain data pipeline](torchtitan/components/data/README.md) with packing, mixing, and checkpointable state - Pretraining, SFT on chat datasets, and LoRA - Muon (DistMuon), EMA, multi-token prediction - Warmup-stable-decay LR schedule and [validation](docs/evaluation.md) **Post-training with [TitanRL](torchtitan/rl/README.md)** - One model definition shared by the trainer and vLLM - [Bitwise trainer/generator parity](torchtitan/rl/BITWISE_PARITY.md) in batch-invariant mode - Async rollouts orchestrated with Monarch; trainer-to-generator model state dict transfer over TorchStore - GRPO and DAPO losses; [DAPO Math](torchtitan/rl/examples/dapo_math), [Search-R1](torchtitan/rl/examples/search_r1), and [Verifiers](torchtitan/rl/examples/verifiers) examples **Checkpointing** - [Distributed checkpointing](torchtitan/components/checkpointer/README.md), including async saves - Load and save Hugging Face safetensors directly - [Conversion scripts](scripts/checkpoint_conversion) between HF and DCP **Debugging and observability** - [Metrics](torchtitan/observability/METRICS.md): loss, memory, throughput, TFLOPs, and MFU in TensorBoard or W&B - [Profiling and memory snapshots](torchtitan/observability/README.md) - [Flight Recorder and other debugging tools](docs/debugging.md) - Fake-backend dry runs of large layouts on one GPU - Deterministic mode and [loss comparison](scripts/loss_compare.py) across commits - [SDC replay](torchtitan/observability/SILENT_DATA_CORRUPTION.md) and [structured logging](torchtitan/observability/structured_logger/README.md) **Extensibility** - Python [recipes](torchtitan/config/README.md) selected with `--module` and `--config` - [Component overrides](torchtitan/config/OVERRIDE.md) for custom kernels and modules - [Experiments](torchtitan/experiments): GraphTrainer, TorchFT, Transformers modeling backend
We report [performance](docs/benchmarks/llama3_h100_202412_torchtitan.md) on up to 512 GPUs and verify [loss convergence](torchtitan/models/llama3/README.md#loss-convergence) across parallelisms and | ## Installation The [quick start](#quick-start) installs from source, which is the recommended way to get the latest features. Other options:
Nightly builds ```bash pip install --pre torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/nightly/cu132 --force-reinstall pip install --pre torchtitan --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/nightly/cu132 ``` Replace `cu132` with another CUDA version or a ROCm build (e.g. `rocm10.0`).
Stable releases ```bash pip install torchtitan # or conda install conda-forge::torchtitan ``` Each stable release pins the nightly versions of `torch` and `torchao` it was validated against; see [RELEASE.md](RELEASE.md).
Optional dependencies - **Low precision (MXFP8, NVFP4):** install the `torchao` nightly CI pins, from the index matching your `torch` build. It is not in `requirements.txt` so it cannot be resolved against a different `torch`: ```bash USE_CPP=0 pip install --pre -r .github/requirements-torchao.txt --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/nightly/cu132 ``` - **RL:** `scripts/install_rl_env.sh` installs the vLLM, Monarch, and TorchStore nightlies and the FlashAttention build for your GPU. See the [RL quick start](torchtitan/rl/README.md#quick-start). - **Extras** for vision, FLUX, RL, and development are also available as `pip install -e ".[vlm,flux,rl,dev]"`. - **Importing from elsewhere:** the source tree runs as is; to import `torchtitan` from another directory, install it in editable mode without re-resolving dependencies: `pip install -e . --no-deps`.
Multi-node training with Slurm Submit [`scripts/multinode_trainer.slurm`](scripts/multinode_trainer.slurm) with `sbatch` from the repository root. Set the node count in both the `#SBATCH` header and the `torchrun --nnodes` argument: ```bash #SBATCH --ntasks=2 #SBATCH --nodes=2 srun torchrun --nnodes 2 ... ``` If a node does not have 8 GPUs, also adjust `--nproc_per_node` and `#SBATCH --gpus-per-task`.
